title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
statement_short: Given an array of integers nums sorted in non-decreasing order, find the starting and ending position of a given target value. If target is not found in the array, return [-1, -1]. Write an algorithm with O(log n) runtime complexity.
constraints: 0 <= nums.length <= 10^5, -10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9, nums is sorted in non-decreasing order, -10^9 <= target <= 10^9
hint: Array length up to 10^5 and strict O(log n) requirement mandate running two binary searches for left and right boundary indices.
why_not: Right: Binary Search ran twice (lower bound and upper bound) finds exact start and end target boundaries in O(log n) time and O(1) space. Not Two Pointers: Finding target and expanding outward with two pointers takes O(n) worst-case time when all elements equal target. Not Sliding Window: Sliding window techniques compute contiguous subsegment totals rather than finding exact boundary indices. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Hash maps track first/last indices in O(n) space and time.
